text:
Philip Rubin obtained his BA in psychology and linguistics from Brandeis University in 1971 and earned his PhD in experimental psychology from the University of Connecticut in 1975. His research spans multiple fields, utilizing computational, engineering, linguistic, physiological, and psychological methods to study embodied cognition, particularly the biological foundations of speech and language.
His key contributions include work on articulatory synthesis and speech perception, involving the design of computational models such as ASY and SWS. Rubin is noted for designing and implementing the approach for describing and controlling articulatory events, now known as speech gestures. Furthermore, he was instrumental in the development of the HADES signal processing system and the SPIEL programming language. He also served in leadership roles in science administration and policy, including as the Director of the Division of Behavioral and Cognitive Sciences at the National Science Foundation (NSF) from 2000 to 2003.
